home.differenceHeadline: A written plan before the sign goes up
home.differenceBody:
Listing a home you have lived in for years is a lot to hand over to someone. You should know what happens on day one, day three and day ten before you agree to any of it.

That is the whole idea. A walkthrough, an honest fix-or-skip list, a price you understand, and a launch scheduled to the day.

faq.q: What should I fix before I sell?
faq.a: Often less than you think. After the walkthrough you get a written fix-or-skip list, so you only spend money on what will come back to you.

faq.q: How do you decide the listing price?
faq.a: We put recent nearby sales next to your home on one page and decide together. You will understand the number before it goes on the listing.

faq.q: How much disruption will showings be?
faq.a: The showing schedule is part of the ten-day plan, agreed before launch, so you know when people are coming through.

faq.q: How will I know what is happening once it is listed?
faq.a: You get a short written update every week: who came through, what they said, and the next step.

faq.q: Do you work with buyers too?
faq.a: Yes, especially first-time buyers in Elk Grove and South Sacramento who want each step explained.

leadMagnet.title: The Before-You-List Checklist
leadMagnet.subtitle: What to fix, what to skip, and what to do in the 30 days before your Sacramento home goes on the market.
leadMagnet.hook: The money most sellers waste is spent before the listing goes live. This checklist shows where.
bullets: The repairs that usually pay you back, and the ones that rarely do
The questions to ask any agent before you sign
leadMagnet.formHeadline: Where should I send your checklist?
leadMagnet.thankYou: Your checklist is ready below. A copy is on its way to your inbox.

sections.heading: 1. Walk it like a buyer
sections.body: Start at the curb and walk in the way a buyer would. Write down the first five things you notice. Those are the five things a buyer notices too.

sections.heading: 2. Fix: what usually pays
sections.body: Fresh paint in tired rooms, working light fixtures, doors that close properly, and a tidy front entry. Small, cheap, and seen in every photo.

sections.heading: 3. Skip: what rarely pays
sections.body: Full kitchen remodels, new flooring throughout, and anything that takes longer than the listing timeline. Buyers often want to choose those themselves.

sections.heading: 4. The 30-day countdown
sections.body:
Day 30: walkthrough and fix-or-skip list.
Day 21: repairs booked.
Day 10: declutter and deep clean.
Day 3: photos.
Day 0: listing goes live.

sections.heading: 5. Questions to ask any agent
sections.body: What happens in the first ten days? How will you price it, and can I see the numbers? How often will I hear from you, and how?

sections.heading: 6. Your paperwork pile
sections.body: Gather permits for past work, utility costs for the last year, and any warranties. Having them ready answers buyer questions before they are asked.

leadMagnet.closing: Want the walkthrough done with you? Reply to the email this came with and we will find a time.

audit.summary: Sellers are looking for you online, and right now there is nowhere for them to land, and nothing to catch them when they do.

opportunities.title: No way to capture leads
opportunities.why: Referrals are great, but the sellers who are a year out are searching quietly. Without a free offer, they never become a name you can follow up with.
opportunities.evidence: You told us you have no free guide or opt-in, and new clients come from referrals and open houses.
opportunities.whatChanges: Every month, the people thinking about selling raise their hand by asking for your checklist.
opportunities.bossDoes: Lead magnets, landing pages and funnels built from one set of answers, connected to follow-up that sends itself.

opportunities.title: Invisible to Google and AI assistants
opportunities.why: With only a brokerage profile, an AI assistant asked for an East Sac listing agent has nothing of yours to recommend.
opportunities.evidence: You have no website of your own. The competitor site we checked has structured data on none of its pages and no Equal Housing statement.
opportunities.whatChanges: A site of your own, built to the launch bar, that Google and AI assistants can read and recommend.
opportunities.bossDoes: A site built to our launch bar, structured data on every page, checked and fixed automatically, with articles written to be recommended by AI.

opportunities.title: Leads go cold
opportunities.why: Sellers often take months to decide. Inconsistent follow-up means someone else is there when they are ready.
opportunities.evidence: You said follow-up with people who are not ready yet is inconsistent.
opportunities.whatChanges: Everyone who asks for the checklist hears from you on day 0, 2 and 5 without you lifting a finger.
opportunities.bossDoes: Follow-up sequences in your voice that run on their own.

moreMagnets.title: The First-Time Buyer's Elk Grove Starter Guide
moreMagnets.subtitle: Every step from your first lender call to the keys, explained in plain words.
moreMagnets.hook: Most first-time buyers are not short on homes to look at. They are short on someone explaining what happens next.
bullets: The questions to ask a lender before you look at a single home
A written timeline from inspection to keys
moreMagnets.formHeadline: Where should I send your guide?

sections.heading: 1. Before you look
sections.body:
Talk to a lender first, and ask:
- What monthly payment am I comfortable with, not just approved for?
- What will closing cost me, roughly?
- How long is my pre-approval good for?

sections.heading: 2. Looking at homes
sections.body: Bring a short list of must-haves and a shorter list of deal-breakers. Photos do not show noise, smells or light: visit at two different times of day.

sections.heading: 3. Making an offer
sections.body: An offer is more than a price. It covers deposits, inspection time, financing time and closing date. You should understand every term before you sign.

sections.heading: 4. Inspection to keys
sections.body:
[ ] Inspection booked
[ ] Appraisal ordered
[ ] Insurance quote
[ ] Final walkthrough
[ ] Keys
